title: How I changed how I use AI for Stock Research
author: SnowSilent7695
selftext:
For over a year, I've used Claude and ChatGPT to help with stock research and both have been great. The thing I've always wanted from these, however, is to actively monitor market during the day, when I'm busy, and build a dashboard that updates automatically that I can come back to anytime without having to ask follow up questions.

I think this is where the field is headed and wanted to share an example of how I use Claude to currently do this--"Can you stream live updates for the biggest movers, losers and earnings announcements and financial releases (8K, investor relation materials, etc). Please create a dashboard with key highlights and an event stream. Keep the stream going throughout the day,"

It's been great surfacing stocks and things that I normally wouldn't think of (e.g. KMX which had a strong quarter and great year so far) that helps me expand my portfolio.

A big thing I wanted to solve for is token consumption. I've used Anthropic's equity agents in the past, and while phenomenal, they burn through tokens. With this, Claude just opens up a live stream of whatever I want to subscribe to and things are posted to a dashboard or whatever Claude built on the fly, with no further polling, processing, prompting, etc. on Claude's side.

comments.author: SnowSilent7695
comments.body:
I've codified this into a workflow that let's Claude (or any AI Agent) just listen to the market and report back. Anyone is welcome to try it in Claude through its connectors: add custom connection > in remote server url [https://mcp.flexreportfinapi.com/mcp](https://mcp.flexreportfinapi.com/mcp)

The codebase for the workflow is also public, which highlights other use-cases and allows you to modify it and make it your own: [https://github.com/cbecks1212/flexreport-mcp](https://github.com/cbecks1212/flexreport-mcp)

The main goal is to make staying on top of the market scalable and accessible to everyone

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body:
The token-efficiency point is the key design win. Having the agent subscribe to a stream instead of polling means the model only spends tokens when something actually happens. One tip for making a dashboard like that more useful: attach context to each item as it arrives, such as the event type, its exact release time, and whether it was a beat or miss vs. expectations. A raw stream of 8-Ks and press releases still forces the model to work out what matters and when, which is where mistakes creep in (a late-evening filing read as pre-close news, for instance).

That structured, timestamped layer is what we build at Cymetica with EventTrader, and it fits the same "listen, then reason" pattern you describe.

Nice touch on open-sourcing the workflow, too.

comments.author: AcanthocephalaNo6605
comments.body:
Ideally you need to have a integrated workspace where your AI, market data API, scripts and order routing is under one hood. Then only the whole system can be automated.

Now this is more challenging to make underlying platform to have all this in single workspace with out any integration issues.

We had the same issue and that let to an Idea of making while25: A programmable trading platform. It has inbuilt agent which can monitor but the good part is your data is wired using API and on top of that you can use while25 python sdk to streamline the data for your agent so it barely consume 100 tokens on each call which is dirt cheap.

You can look at it here: https://while25.com
